title: t2 (null: task-shuffled): priority-max over 5 symbols, read out by head 3.1
label: function verified against the model's own outputs; dataset labels are shuffled; circuit effect sizes weak
behavior: BOS + 5 tokens from 6 symbols (bo=1, la=3, nu=4, pa=5, ri=6, vu=7); the model emits one symbol at the last position.
summary: All numbers are from local-full (full precision). The answer labels that the lab scores against in this investigation are NOT the model's outputs: the model matches them on only 42-54% of prompts (E0002, E0004, V0001: 44.5%), and when I supplied my own labels the lab scored against a permuted version of them (E0005). There is therefore no label-following behaviour to explain, and every logit-diff number here is measured against shuffled labels. The model itself is deterministic and computes a clean function: it outputs the highest-priority symbol present, with priority bo > nu > pa > la > ri > vu. That rule equals the model's actual output on 200/200 held-out prompts (V0001; shuffled-label null p95 = 0.465). Eleven of the sixteen components are exactly inert (E0008, V0001). The remaining five - mlp0, mlp1, head 2.0, mlp2, head 3.1 - are the only ones whose ablation changes outputs; head 3.1 is the read-out and attends from the last position to the winner's position with weight 0.9999 (E0011). Three of six pre-registered predictions were refuted, two of them (E0002, E0005) because of the shuffled labels.

claims.text: The lab's answer labels in this investigation are decoupled from the model's outputs: the model matches them on 42% (seed 1), 54% (seed 0) and 44.5% (seed 7) of prompts, with per-prompt logit diffs of exactly +1/-1/0.

Labels supplied explicitly are also permuted before scoring: on 24 hand-built prompts the 'expected' tokens shown differ from the ones I passed, while the model's printed outputs equal the priority-rule answers.

The model computes: output the highest-priority symbol present among the five inputs, priority bo(1) > nu(4) > pa(5) > la(3) > ri(6) > vu(7). The rule equals the model's actual output on 200/200 held-out prompts, above every shuffled-label null (max 0.485).
Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.0, 3.2 and mlp3 play no part: mean-ablating all of them together leaves the metric exactly unchanged (fraction 1.000) on seed 0 and on held-out seed 7.
Head 3.1 is the read-out: from the last position it attends with weight 0.9999 to the position that holds the winning symbol (12 hand-built prompts, winner at position 2; uniform would be 0.17).

mlp0, mlp1, head 2.0, mlp2 and head 3.1 are the only components whose ablation changes the outputs; ablating the five together drops the held-out metric to 24.5% of clean (97th percentile of the null), but that metric is only 0.06 against shuffled labels and my own pre-registered collapse prediction on seed 0 failed (48% left).

nodes.label: head 2.0: BOS + other positions, never self
head 3.1: last pos -> winner's position, copies symbol

edges.label: order inferred from layer index only
presumably selects where 3.1 looks; not path-patched

limitations: Every logit-diff metric in this investigation is scored against shuffled labels, so causal effect sizes (E0006, E0007, E0009, V0001 necessity/sufficiency) are small and noisy; only 'exactly unchanged' results and the predict-vs-model agreement are label-independent.

Pre-registered prediction E0009 (joint ablation of the five active components collapses the metric to <=10%) was refuted: 48% remained. With shuffled labels a constant output still scores a non-zero logit diff, so this neither confirms nor rules out that ablating the five destroys the behaviour.
The single-component ablation sweeps (E0006, E0007) and the head 2.0 attention pattern (E0010) are exploratory.
The internal roles of mlp0, mlp1, head 2.0 and mlp2 were not measured; the edges between them in the diagram are ordering by layer, not path-patching results.
The gradient screen E0003 pointed at head 3.1 and mlp3 only; mlp3 turned out to be exactly inert and three MLPs it scored at zero matter. Attribution patching is unreliable on this model.
V0001's three random same-size control sets all gave fraction 1.000, which suggests they were drawn from non-circuit components; they do not test much.

The priority order was read from the dataset listing and confirmed by agreement on 200 random prompts; prompts containing only ri/vu are rare (about 0.4%), so the ri > vu end of the order rests on few cases (one in E0001, two printed in E0005).
open_questions: What do mlp0, mlp1, head 2.0 and mlp2 compute? Head 2.0's pattern (BOS plus other positions, zero on self) and 3.1's rank-like lookup are compatible with a sort (count how many tokens outrank me, then look up by rank), but that was not tested.
With faithful labels, how large is the drop when the five components are ablated?
overall_status: verified · function verified against the model's own outputs; dataset labels are shuffled; circuit effect sizes weak

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model deterministically performs the bench behaviour: on the bench dataset its top token at the last position matches the dataset answer (its own outputs) with a positive logit difference.

prediction.statement: Clean accuracy on the bench dataset is at least 98%.

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: H1: the model outputs the highest-priority symbol present, priority bo(1) > nu(4) > pa(5) > la(3) > ri(6) > vu(7). On 24 hand-built prompts covering every adjacent priority pair, all-same inputs and the rare ri/vu-only cases, with labels computed from H1, the model is right every time.

prediction.statement: With H1-derived labels the model is correct on all 24 hand-built prompts.

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: H2 active set: mlp0, mlp1, head 2.0, mlp2 and head 3.1 carry the computation: mean-ablating them together makes the output input-independent, so the metric collapses to about zero.

prediction.statement: Joint mean ablation of the five claimed-active components leaves at most 10% of the clean metric.
